question: Will rhinovirus account for more than 53.5% of SRAG cases with positive viral results over the last four epidemiological weeks in InfoGripe's epidemiological week 44 bulletin (released 12 November 2026)?

calls.reasoning: The four-week rhinovirus share in recent bulletins was 51.6 (SE37), 52.5 (SE39), 53.0 (SE40), 53.7 (SE41) and 53.3 (SE42). The threshold of 53.5 sits about 0.2pp above the latest value, so this is close to a coin flip. Two-week changes in the series have ranged from -0.4 to +1.2pp. Between SE40 and SE42, RSV fell from 14.3 to 11.5 and metapneumovirus is falling, which frees share for rhinovirus. Pushing the other way, flu A rose from 2.8 to 4.1, SARS-CoV-2 rose from 4.8 to 6.4, and Covid is described as rising slightly. Rhinovirus is described as stable nationally. Tail risk from a late-year influenza A surge (as in 2025, when rhinovirus was 37.8% in the SE46 bulletin) skews slightly toward No. No human market was found: the harness search of Polymarket/Manifold found nothing and no Kalshi or bookmaker market came up (not searched separately).

calls.dossier:
- Resolves off the InfoGripe Resumo for SE 44 (Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_44.pdf, due Thu 12 Nov 2026), using the four-week share of rhinovirus among POSITIVE SRAG CASES, not deaths. Threshold is >53.5 for Yes; 53.5 exactly resolves No.
- Event window: the SE44 bulletin's four-week window is SE41-44 (11 Oct -> 7 Nov 2026). As of Now (2 Nov 2026) about 3 of those 4 weeks have elapsed, but the data are incomplete; the bulletin itself is still 10 days away.
- Four-week rhinovirus series (question background and Fiocruz news): SE37 51.6, SE39 52.5, SE40 53.0, SE41 53.7, SE42 53.3. Two-week changes observed: +0.9 (SE37->39), +1.2 (SE39->41), +0.3 (SE40->42); one-week change SE41->42 was -0.4.
- SE40 bulletin (Fiocruz news, Oct 2026): rhinovirus 53.0, RSV 14.3, flu B 5.7, SARS-CoV-2 4.8, flu A 2.8. Rhinovirus increases were concentrated in MG, PR and SP; metapneumovirus was expanding in the Centre-South and Northeast; flu B was decelerating in BA but slightly resurging in RS.
- SE42 bulletin (released 29 Oct 2026; BVS/Fiocruz coverage): rhinovirus 53.3, RSV 11.5, flu B 5.4, SARS-CoV-2 6.4, flu A 4.1. Nationally: metapneumovirus falling, rhinovirus stable, Covid-19 rising slightly from a low base. SRAG shows short-term growth and long-term stabilization or oscillation.
- SE42 state drivers: MT mainly SARS-CoV-2; MS rhinovirus plus SARS-CoV-2; SE metapneumovirus; AP and MA have insufficient lab data. Metapneumovirus is rising in SP, RJ, BA, PE and SE even though it is falling nationally.
- SE40->SE42 shifts in competing viruses: RSV -2.8pp, SARS-CoV-2 +1.6pp, flu A +1.3pp, flu B -0.3pp. The four-week sentence does not list metapneumovirus, which is part of the remaining ~19%.
- 2025 analogue: the mid-November 2025 bulletin (SE46) had rhinovirus 37.8% and flu A 25.3%. A late-year influenza A wave can rapidly displace the rhinovirus share.
- The MoH Informe de Síndromes Gripais (47% rhinovirus over SE38-41) uses different windows and is not the resolution source.
- Reporting lag: the last two weeks of each bulletin are incomplete, so the share shifts with both revisions and newly added weeks.
- Searched but not found: the SE43 bulletin (not yet released; URL 404 as of 2 Nov); text of the SE41 PDF; any national influenza A growth signal for late Oct 2026. Market check: no Polymarket/Manifold market (harness search); no Kalshi or bookmaker market came up (not searched separately).
calls.reference_class: Two-week changes in the InfoGripe four-week rhinovirus share across SE37-SE42 2026 bulletins, relative to a threshold set near the current level

calls.reasoning: Rhinovirus four-week share was 53.3% in the SE42 bulletin; the threshold of 53.5% needs a rise of more than 0.2pp over two bulletin steps. The series drifted up (51.6 at SE37 to 53.7 at SE41) but dipped at SE42. Two-week changes have been about +0.3 to +1.2pp, so noise is similar in size to the gap. Covid (4.8 to 6.4%) and influenza A (2.8 to 4.1%) are rising and erode rhinovirus's share, offset by falling RSV and influenza B. Fiocruz calls rhinovirus stable nationally. In mid-November 2025 an influenza A wave sharply cut rhinovirus's share. Net: slightly below a coin flip. No human market found (harness found none on Polymarket/Manifold; I did not search Kalshi or bookmakers myself).

calls.reasoning: Rhinovirus 4-week share was 53.3% at SE42 versus a 53.5% threshold, after a slow climb from 51.6% (SE37) to 53.7% (SE41) and a -0.4 dip. Fiocruz calls it stable nationally. Covid and flu A are each up 1.3-1.6pp over two bulletins, offsetting falling RSV and metapneumovirus. The shift needed (+0.3pp over two steps) is within normal noise. A late-year flu A rebound like 2025's only pushes toward No, and a tie at 53.5% resolves No. Net: slightly below a coin flip.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs reported the same facts: the series 51.6/52.5/53.0/53.7/53.3, the SE40 and SE42 virus mixes, SE43 not yet published, and no market found. They differed only in weighting (0.42-0.46). No factual dispute needed settling, and without web access I could not check the SE43 figure. I take the No-leaning reading: the threshold is above the latest value, competing viruses are rising, the influenza tail risk is one-sided, and a tie resolves No.
